newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch state cuts stake in KLM to 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch state cuts stake in KLM to 25 pct.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines and the Dutch government said on Thursday they had agreed in principle that KLM would buy back some 17.3 million ordinary shares held by the state.
The shares would be converted into a new class of shares and withdrawn, the two said in a joint statement.
The move will cut the Dutch state's voting stake in KLM to 25 percent from a current 38.2 percent.
"Underlying the planned conversion and withdrawal of the shares are the wishes of both the State of the Netherlands and KLM to further privatise the airline," the statement said.
It said that under the deal KLM would pay between 900 million guilders and 1.045 billion guilders to the Dutch state.
The final price will based on movements in the KLM share price between December 10 and 13, 1996, reduced by a discount of 2.5 percent.

The deal would be waived should the weighted average of KLM's share price fall below 41.00 guilders or rise above 56.00 guilders during this period. KLM shares were trading 1.80 guilders higher at 47.00 guilders.
Final payment to the state must be made by June 2, 1997.
The sum would be financed entirely from KLM's reserves, the statement added.
